original_question: For the associated-form morphism Phi, define p to be the smallest positive integer such that Delta^p Phi extends from the nondegenerate locus X_n^d to a morphism on the entire affine space of degree-d forms. Compute this integer p.
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the paper’s separate discussion of the contravariant Δ^pΦ—namely, the problem of determining, for each pair (n,d), the minimal exponent p needed to clear the poles of the associated-form morphism Φ and extend it from the nondegenerate locus X_n^d to all degree-d forms. This is distinct from Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3, which concern the invariant-theoretic reconstruction conjecture rather than the exponent p.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the associated-form morphism Φ, the discriminant Δ, the nondegenerate locus X_n^d, and the minimal-exponent extension problem whose solution yields the contravariant Δ^pΦ.
missing_details: p is not a single universal integer; it depends on the fixed pair (n,d).
The ambient field should be specified as \u211a.

The affine space should be named precisely: \u211a-space \u211a? No; in the paper it is the vector space \u211a-space of forms \mathcal{Q}_n^d, i.e. homogeneous degree-d forms in n variables on \u211a^n.
The degree restrictions n \ge 2 and d \ge 3 are part of the setup.
The nondegenerate locus must be defined explicitly as X_n^d := {f \in \mathcal{Q}_n^d : \Delta(f) \neq 0}.
The codomain of Φ should be stated: \Phi : X_n^d \to \mathcal{Q}_n^{n(d-2)*}, the space of degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space.
The discriminant \Delta should be identified as the discriminant on \mathcal{Q}_n^d.
The paper says 'smallest integer', not 'smallest positive integer'; in principle one should allow p = 0 if extension were already regular.
The phrase 'extends ... to a morphism' should be made precise as a regular morphism \mathcal{Q}_n^d \to \mathcal{Q}_n^{n(d-2)*}, not merely a rational map.
To be paper-faithful, the question should ask to determine p = p(n,d) for fixed n,d, not to 'compute this integer p' as if there were one global value.

The hidden context for Φ is that it is defined via the Milnor algebra of f; for \Delta(f) \neq 0 this algebra is Artinian Gorenstein with nilpotent maximal ideal of socle degree n(d-2), which explains the target degree of the associated form.

The paper does not present a general computation of p; it surveys the problem and known upper bounds. A stand-alone question should therefore be phrased as a determination problem, not as if the answer were already known in the paper.
refined_question: Fix integers n \ge 2 and d \ge 3, let \mathcal{Q}_n^d be the complex vector space of homogeneous degree-d forms on \mathbb{C}^n, let X_n^d := \{f \in \mathcal{Q}_n^d : \Delta(f) \neq 0\} be the discriminant-complement, and let \Phi : X_n^d \to \mathcal{Q}_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism. Determine the smallest integer p = p(n,d) such that the product \Delta^p\Phi extends to a regular morphism \mathcal{Q}_n^d \to \mathcal{Q}_n^{n(d-2)*}.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the exact power of the discriminant needed to realize the associated-form map as a contravariant on all degree-d forms, i.e. the minimal exponent p for which \Delta^p\Phi defines a contravariant on \mathcal{Q}_n^d.
justification: Your draft clearly targets the contravariant-exponent problem attached to the associated-form morphism, because it uses exactly the paper’s definition of p as the minimal power of the discriminant needed to extend \Phi from X_n^d to all of \mathcal{Q}_n^d. That is not the same as the headline invariant-theoretic statement in Conjecture 1.1, nor its reformulation in Proposition 1.2 or reduction in Theorem 1.3; those concern extracting GL_n-invariants from associated forms. The paper’s intent here is narrower: introduce p(n,d), note that \Delta^p\Phi is then a contravariant, and discuss known bounds rather than a full general computation. The main defects in the draft are that it treats p as a single integer instead of a function of (n,d), omits the ambient vector spaces and codomain, and phrases the task as a finished computation rather than the determination problem actually left open in the surrounding discussion.
